authors: Hugo Henri Joseph Senetaire, Damien Garreau, Jes Frellsen, Pierre-Alexandre Mattei
title: Explainability as Statistical Inference
validity_discussion: Uses imputation only as a module to turn off features for feature attribution. Mentions that single deterministic imputation causes class information leakage or poor feature selection, whereas stochastic multiple imputation yields more plausible interpretations. Quote: "Borrowing terminology from the missing data literature, we call single imputations the ones produced by deterministic schemes... and multiple imputations the ones produced by truly stochastic schemes."

title: Handling High-Dimensional Missing Data Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches
validity_discussion: Substantive review comparing statistical, tree-based, and deep learning imputation. Discusses Rubin's framework, item vs. unit nonresponse, MAR mechanisms, and doubly robust estimators, noting that validity depends on model specification. Quote: "The validity of the above methods depend on the underlying outcome regression model and nonresponse model assumptions. Doubly robust approaches... have been proposed to improve the robustness to model misspecification."

authors: Dominic Stefan Bräm, Uri Nahum, Andrew Atkinson, Gilbert Koch, Marc Pfister
title: Evaluation of Machine Learning Methods for Covariate Data Imputation in Pharmacometrics
validity_discussion: Comprehensive simulation study evaluating statistical validity under Rubin's framework (MCAR, MAR). Evaluates parameter bias, standard error inflation, and nominal 95% coverage rates using Rubin's rules. Quote: "Missing data create challenges in clinical research because they lead to loss of statistical power and potentially to biased results... Each complete dataset is then analyzed separately and the results are combined using so-called 'Rubin's rules'... to better consider the uncertainty coming from missing values."

authors: Weinan Dong, Daniel Yee Tak Fong, Jin-sun Yoon, Eric Yuk Fai Wan, Laura Elizabeth Bedford, Eric Ho Man Tang, Cindy Lo Kuen Lam
title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Imputing Missing Data for Big Data Clinical Research
validity_discussion: Mentions MAR/MCAR for missingness simulation, but explicitly disclaims post-imputation statistical inference evaluation, focusing solely on predictive accuracy (NRMSE, PFC). Quote: "First and foremost, this study had only focused on the imputation accuracy but not post-imputation statistical inference effectiveness of different imputation methods. The goal of missing data imputation is to obtain statistically valid inferences from incomplete data rather than to re-create the true data."

title: GAMIN: Generative Adversarial Multiple Imputation Network for Highly Missing Data
validity_discussion: References Rubin's framework and rules to motivate multi-modal sampling and top-k confidence ranking under high missingness (>80%), but evaluates reconstruction RMSE and classification accuracy on images rather than inferential correctness or coverage. Quote: "For multiple imputation, performance metric would follow Rubin’s rules... because Rubin’s rule implies that true multiple imputations are equivalent."
